analysis:
Examined all supplied units and compared troubleshooting BASE/HEAD, recovery code and the bounded ServingReadiness patch. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md:83,143 now distinguish current refusal from stale/unconfirmed evidence, accept a request routed after the latest status as diagnostic routing evidence, and document recovery only while NOT receiving. UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift removes the separate authorization predicate (BASE:42–48); HEAD:26–38 retains idle-only, jittered threshold and exponential retry bounds. The ServingReadiness patch describes diagnostics-only behavior and adds a 60-second refusal lifetime and an unconfirmed verdict. No supplied evidence shows these diagnostic changes granting serving permission, extending Apple proof lifetime, exposing plaintext/keys, or changing billing, cache crypto, artifact verification or privileged-helper controls. Unchanged operational advice and report collection were also examined; they are not new regressions.
Relevant integration concerns are A-018 availability and TB-002/TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-057 authorization boundaries. Review the full ServingReadiness implementation and ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift together: establish that aged refusals reset recovery appropriately without suppressing recovery for genuinely stranded connections, that post-status request evidence is scoped to the current socket and cannot override revocation/expiry in admission, and that unconfirmed remains diagnostic rather than serving authorization. The documented external contract—that legacy authorization sends no updated status while maintained refusals repeat—is not independently verified here. Missing implementation and callers prevent a security conclusion about those interactions; no concrete regression qualifies from this local evidence.
